assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt base_plate to the floor plane, then fasten front_rail, back_rail, left_rail, and right_rail on top of it as the 8.6 m × 5.0 m datum frame. 2. Stand post_front_left, post_front_right, post_back_left, and post_back_right on the rails, then add x_brace_front and x_brace_back so all elevated subassemblies have a visible load path. 3. Mount input_plate and embedding_table at the base and connect them to residual_pipe with embedding_bus. 4. Install residual_pipe vertically through the center and add the eight rendered transformer slices plus layer_count_marker to show the 96-layer deep-narrow stack. 5. Attach the exploded attention subassembly on the viewer-left side of block_03: attn_pre_norm, q_head_fanout, kv_head_bank, qk_norm_disk, rope_disk, attn_kernel, and attn_o_proj; connect it back to residual_pipe with attention_return_bus. 6. Mount the eight kv_cache_cell_* cartridges on the amber cache rail and tie them to kv_cache_bus so the 8 KV-head GQA reduction is visible. 7. Attach the exploded MoE subassembly on the viewer-right side of block_03: ffn_post_norm, moe_router, moe_group_limit, moe_alltoall_dispatch, eight expert_group_* cartridges, moe_shared_expert, moe_group_gemm, fp8_gemm_disk, moe_alltoall_combine, and moe_output_bus. 8. Fasten prediction_head above the stack, then add mtp_head, lm_loss, mtp_loss, mode_think, and mode_no_think as exposed head-side modules. 9. Install training_data_pipe, optimizer_adamw, post_train_rl, and parallelism_marker as external service modules and connect each to the main frame with named bus bars. 10. Verify that every elevated plate is connected to base_frame either through a rail/post or through a named compute bus, and that no explanatory subsystem is hidden inside an opaque enclosure.

info.summary: 355B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model from Zhipu AI / Z.ai (32B activated per token). Deep-and-narrow design: 96 layers × 5120 hidden dim. GQA attention (96 Q heads / 8 KV heads, partial RoPE, QK-Norm), 160 routed + 1 shared expert per layer with sigmoid loss-free routing and group-limited top-8 dispatch, MTP head for speculative decoding, and a hybrid thinking / non-thinking mode that shares weights. Pre-trained on ~23 T tokens, post-trained for agentic + reasoning + coding with self-distillation RL.
info.description:
GLM-4.5 is Z.ai's flagship open MoE for the 'ARC' (Agentic, Reasoning, Coding) trinity. Compared with GLM-4 it is much sparser (only 32B of 355B activated per token), DEEPER (96 layers vs 40) but NARROWER (5120 hidden dim vs 6144), and adds first-class hybrid reasoning: a single set of weights answers either in 'think' or 'no-think' mode controlled by a system prompt. Routing uses a sigmoid gate with the auxiliary-loss-free bias trick (DeepSeek-V3 style) and an extra group-limit constraint (each token may activate experts on AT MOST 4 of 8 device groups), which keeps cross-node all-to-all bounded. QK-Norm + partial RoPE replace V3's full-RoPE on attention. A single Multi-Token Prediction head provides ~1.8× speculative decoding speedup. Training is 3-stage (general → reasoning → long-context) on ~23T tokens, with FP8 GEMMs and BF16 master weights.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• Deep-narrow: more layers ≫ wider FFN per FLOP for reasoning tasks at fixed compute.
• Group-limited routing: caps EP all-to-all bandwidth, the real bottleneck on H800-class clusters.
• Hybrid think mode: avoids maintaining two separate models (chat + reasoning).
• MTP head: free speculative decoding without a draft model.

facts.label: QK norm
facts.value: RMSNorm on Q and K (replaces soft-cap)

comparisons.delta: GLM-4 was a dense decoder (~32B at the upper end). GLM-4.5 jumps to a 355B sparse MoE with 32B activated — same per-token FLOPs but ~11× more capacity. Adds GQA (V4 was MHA), QK-Norm, partial RoPE, MTP, hybrid thinking, and the sigmoid loss-free balance trick. Vocabulary stays in the 150K range.

Two generations of pre-norm dense decoders with full RoPE and bilinear FFN. GLM-4.5 keeps RoPE (partial now) but otherwise replaces every load-bearing block: SwiGLU FFN → MoE with shared expert, MHA → GQA, plain attention → QK-Norm + partial-RoPE, SFT-only post-training → multi-stage RL with self-distillation. Goes from 32K → 128K context.

Same family of ideas (MoE + shared expert + auxiliary-loss-free balancing + MTP) but tuned differently: GLM-4.5 is SMALLER (355B vs 671B), DEEPER (96 vs 61 layers), and uses GQA + partial RoPE + QK-Norm where V3 uses MLA. V3 has 256 experts top-8 with no group constraint; GLM-4.5 has 160 experts top-8 with group-limited routing (≤4 of 8 groups). V3 supports 128K via YaRN; GLM-4.5 also targets 128K. V3 trained in FP8 mixed; GLM-4.5 also uses FP8 GEMMs.

Versus Qwen3-235B-A22B: GLM-4.5 has more total params (355B vs 235B) and more activated (32B vs 22B), more layers (96 vs 94), but fewer experts (160 vs 128, both top-8). Both have hybrid thinking modes. Versus public GPT-4 estimates: GLM-4.5 is much sparser per token (32B activated vs estimated ~280B+ in GPT-4 dense or ~110B in rumoured GPT-4-MoE), uses GQA at extreme ratios (12:1) for cheaper KV, and is open-weight.

parts.name: Grounded Datum Plate
parts.role: Floor datum for the exposed GLM-4.5 teaching model; all structural rails bolt to this 8.6 m by 5.0 m plate.

parts.name: Front Frame Rail
parts.role: Front rail carries the front posts and keeps the lower token path aligned with the tower.

parts.name: Back Frame Rail
parts.role: Back rail mirrors the front rail and gives the side modules a visible support edge.

parts.name: Left Frame Rail
parts.role: Left rail supports the GQA and KV-cache side assemblies.

parts.name: Right Frame Rail
parts.role: Right rail supports the routed-expert and parallelism side assemblies.

parts.name: Front Left Post
parts.role: Vertical support post for the left-front side of the exploded architecture frame.

parts.name: Front Right Post
parts.role: Vertical support post for the right-front side of the exploded architecture frame.

parts.name: Back Left Post
parts.role: Vertical support post for the left-back side of the frame and KV-cache rail.

parts.name: Back Right Post
parts.role: Vertical support post for the right-back side of the frame and MoE expert bank.

parts.name: Front Cross Brace
parts.role: Diagonal front brace makes the abstract tower read as a buildable framed assembly.

parts.name: Back Cross Brace
parts.role: Diagonal back brace ties the upper side modules back to the grounded datum plate.

parts.name: Input Tokens (BPE)
parts.role: Token-ID stream plate for the 151,552-token BPE vocabulary, feeding integer IDs into the embedding slab.
parts.algorithm:
tokens = bpe.encode(text)
batch = pack(tokens, max_len=32768)
mask = sample_attention_mask(batch)
parts.bottleneck: Loader-side BPE throughput on the CPU.

parts.name: Embedding (V=151K, d=5120)
parts.role: Token-embedding lookup slab tied to the LM head, representing about 776M parameters or 1.55 GiB in BF16.

parts.name: Embedding-to-Residual Bus
parts.role: Short vertical bus showing the first activation transfer from embedding space into the central residual stream.

parts.name: Residual Stream (d=5120, 96 layers)
parts.role: Central pre-norm residual stream carrying d=5120 activations through all 96 transformer layers.
parts.memory_footprint: B·T·d × dtype per layer of activation
parts.algorithm:
x = x + attn(rmsnorm_pre(x))
x = x + ffn(rmsnorm_post(x))

parts.name: Layer Count Spine: 96 Transformer Blocks
parts.role: Etched spine marks the unrendered layers 7 through 94 between the visible early and final slices.
parts.bottleneck: PP bubble across 96 layers unless 1F1B or DualPipe scheduling is used.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 1
parts.role: First visible decoder block slice containing pre-norm GQA attention followed by MoE FFN.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 2
parts.role: Second visible decoder block slice showing the repeated layer recipe at the same width.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 3 Exploded
parts.role: Third visible block is the exploded reference layer whose attention and MoE internals are pulled outward.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 4
parts.role: Fourth visible decoder block slice confirms the uniform deep-and-narrow stack pitch.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 5
parts.role: Fifth visible decoder block slice keeps the layer stack readable without enclosing the pipe.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 6
parts.role: Sixth visible decoder block slice precedes the elided middle layers on the count spine.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 95
parts.role: Penultimate visible block marks the upper end of the 96-layer stack after the elided middle span.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 96 Final
parts.role: Final transformer block slice feeds the tied LM head and auxiliary MTP head.

parts.name: Attention Pre-RMSNorm Gamma Plate
parts.role: Learned RMSNorm gamma plate normalizes the residual stream before QKV projection in each attention sublayer.
parts.algorithm: x_hat = x / sqrt(mean(x*x) + eps); y = gamma * x_hat

parts.name: 96 Query-Head Fanout Comb
parts.role: Wide comb represents Q projection to 96 heads of 128 channels each.

parts.name: 8 KV-Head Bank
parts.role: Narrow bank represents K and V projection to only 8 grouped-query heads, a 12:1 sharing ratio against Q.
parts.algorithm: K = x @ W_K; V = x @ W_V

parts.name: QK-Norm Disk
parts.role: Flat disk marks per-head RMSNorm applied to Q and K before the attention dot product.

parts.name: Partial RoPE Half-Channel Ring
parts.role: Torus marks rotary position encoding applied to 64 of each 128 head channels.

parts.name: FlashAttention-2 Core
parts.role: Dense causal FlashAttention core streams Q, K, and V tiles through SRAM without storing the full attention matrix.
parts.algorithm: attn = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_h)); out = attn @ V

parts.name: Attention O-Projection Plate
parts.role: Output projection plate maps concatenated attention heads back to d=5120 before residual addition.

parts.name: Attention Residual Return Bus
parts.role: Horizontal bus shows the attention output being added back into the central residual pipe.

parts.name: KV Cache Manifold
parts.role: Vertical manifold collects the eight GQA KV cache cartridges for prefill writes and decode reads.
parts.memory_footprint: ≈ 2 KB / token / layer at 8 KV heads and FP8
parts.bottleneck: HBM capacity sets max batchable context per GPU.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 1
parts.role: First visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 2
parts.role: Second visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 3
parts.role: Third visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 4
parts.role: Fourth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 5
parts.role: Fifth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 6
parts.role: Sixth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 7
parts.role: Seventh visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 8
parts.role: Eighth visible KV-head cache cell completes the 8-head GQA cache set.

parts.name: FFN Post-Attention RMSNorm Plate
parts.role: RMSNorm plate normalizes the residual stream before the sparse MoE feed-forward sublayer.
parts.algorithm: x_hat = x / sqrt(mean(x*x) + eps); y = gamma * x_hat

parts.name: Top-8 Sigmoid Router
parts.role: Router disk scores 160 experts with sigmoid gates and selects the top eight experts per token.
parts.algorithm: scores = sigmoid(x @ W_router) + b_balance; topk = topk(scores, 8)
parts.bottleneck: Router is sequential with the following all-to-all dispatch.

parts.name: Group-Limited Routing Ring
parts.role: Ring enforces the rule that a token may activate experts in no more than four of eight device groups.
parts.algorithm: skip expert e if group(e) would exceed the 4-group budget

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Dispatch Ring
parts.role: Dispatch ring represents the NCCL all-to-all that buckets tokens by selected expert before grouped GEMM.
parts.bottleneck: Cross-node InfiniBand traffic and skew-induced stragglers.

parts.name: Expert Group 1 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 of the 160 routed experts for expert-parallel placement.

parts.name: Expert Group 2 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and can be one of the four allowed groups for a token.

parts.name: Expert Group 3 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and exposes the MoE bank as separate hardware lanes.

parts.name: Expert Group 4 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and completes the typical four-group budget example.

parts.name: Expert Group 5 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts that remain available but may be skipped by the group limiter.

parts.name: Expert Group 6 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and shows that the full bank spans eight groups.

parts.name: Expert Group 7 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and provides a visible inactive contrast to the selected lanes.

parts.name: Expert Group 8 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds the final 20 routed experts in the 160-expert MoE layer.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 1
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows one of the eight top-k routed expert calls for the current token.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 2
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows a second top-k expert call sharing the grouped GEMM bed.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 3
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows a third selected expert in the top-8 dispatch set.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 4
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows the fourth selected expert group allowed by the group limiter.

parts.name: Shared Expert Always-On Block
parts.role: Always-on shared expert carries common computation in parallel with the eight routed experts.

parts.name: Grouped GEMM Expert Bed
parts.role: Grouped GEMM bed fuses capacity-padded SwiGLU expert matrix multiplications into one kernel launch.
parts.algorithm: H = silu(X @ W_gate) * (X @ W_up); O = H @ W_down

parts.name: FP8 GEMM Precision Disk
parts.role: Precision marker shows FP8 E4M3 forward and E5M2 backward GEMMs with BF16 master weights.
parts.memory_footprint: FP8 forward weights are about 2× smaller than BF16.

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Combine Ring
parts.role: Combine ring represents the return all-to-all that sends expert outputs back to their original token order.
parts.bottleneck: Cross-node combine latency can stall the residual update.

parts.name: MoE Residual Return Bus
parts.role: Return bus carries the combined MoE output back into the central residual pipe.

parts.name: LM Head Tied with Embedding
parts.role: Tied output projection maps final hidden states back to the 151,552-token vocabulary.

parts.name: MTP Head Depth 1
parts.role: Single multi-token-prediction head supplies speculative decoding targets for about 1.8× inference speedup.
parts.flops_per_token: ≈ one extra block plus LM head GEMM

parts.name: Primary Cross-Entropy Loss
parts.role: Primary next-token cross-entropy loss node supervises the tied LM head during training.

parts.name: Auxiliary MTP Loss
parts.role: Small auxiliary loss trains the MTP head to predict an additional future token.

parts.name: Think Mode Selector
parts.role: Mode plate represents system-prompt selection for chain-of-thought reasoning with a larger decode budget.

parts.name: No-Think Mode Selector
parts.role: Mode plate represents direct-answer prompting that shares weights but uses a smaller reasoning budget.

parts.name: 23T-Token Curriculum Feed
parts.role: Data feed plate represents about 23 trillion tokens across general, reasoning, and long-context training stages.

parts.name: AdamW Optimizer Station
parts.role: Optimizer station stores Adam moments and BF16 master weights for the full 355B-parameter model.
parts.memory_footprint: Adam state stores m and v, roughly 2× parameter size before sharding.
parts.algorithm: m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g; v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g*g; W -= lr*mhat/(sqrt(vhat)+eps)

parts.name: Self-Distillation RL Station
parts.role: Post-training station represents SFT plus self-distillation RL rollouts for agentic, reasoning, and coding tasks.
parts.algorithm: rollouts = sample(policy, prompts); rewards = score(rollouts); loss = grpo_loss(rollouts, rewards)

parts.name: TP × EP × PP × DP Parallelism Board
parts.role: Parallelism board maps tensor, expert, pipeline, and data parallel axes onto the visible attention, MoE, layer, and optimizer modules.
parts.algorithm: rank = (dp, pp, ep, tp); experts assigned by EP group; layers split across PP stages
